title: Career clarity
_README: A branching, curated coaching flow. Every node is authored — nothing is generated. 'type' is one of: statement, choice, freeText, socratic, reframe, action, end. 'next' points to a node id; choice options carry their own 'next'. Optional 'setPattern' tags a pattern when a branch is taken. Optional 'requireAction' marks the closing concrete step. Keep node ids unique within the file.

intro.body: Career clarity rarely arrives as a lightning bolt. It's usually a few honest answers you've been avoiding. Let's find the real question under the noise. This won't tell you what to do — it'll help you hear what you already suspect.

whats_the_itch.prompt: What's actually pulling at you right now?

options.label: I might be on the wrong path entirely
Right path, but I'm stalled and restless
I have options and can't choose
I'm doing fine but feel unseen / undervalued

wrong_path_probe.prompt: When you imagine staying on this path for three more years, what's the strongest feeling?

dread_reframe.body: Dread about the future is data, not weakness. It's usually pointing at a value being crowded out. Notice you said 'quiet' — you've been keeping it quiet, which takes energy.

guilt_reframe.body: Wanting something different isn't a betrayal of the people who helped you get here. Their investment was in you, not in a specific job title. You're allowed to have wanted this once and want something else now.

numb_socratic.body: Numb is often the sound of a feeling that got no reply for a long time.

value_crowded.prompt: Finish this honestly: 'The part of me that's gone quiet in this work is the part that cares about ______.'

clarify_value.body: Hold onto that word. Clarity isn't picking the perfect job — it's refusing to keep abandoning that part of you. Any good next step protects it a little more than the last.

stalled_probe.prompt: Be precise: is this a motivation problem or a permission problem?

options.label: I don't feel like doing the work
I'm waiting for someone to say I'm allowed
I'm scared I'll try and it won't be enough

motivation_socratic.body: Motivation usually follows action, not the other way round. The question is what tiny action you could take before you feel ready.

permission_reframe.body: If you're waiting for permission, notice you've handed someone else the pen to your life. Sometimes the whole move is deciding you're the one who signs off.

perfection_reframe.body: 'Not enough' is perfectionism setting a bar so high that not trying feels safer than trying. But you can't steer a parked car. A messy attempt gives you something real to adjust; a perfect plan in your head gives you nothing.

choose_probe.prompt: You said you can't choose. Name the option you keep circling back to — the one you'd pick if you had to answer in five seconds.

choose_reframe.body: You just answered in five seconds. Often the indecision isn't lack of an answer — it's reluctance to lose the options you'd give up. Choosing costs you the other doors. That grief is real, and it's not a reason to stay frozen at the crossroads.

undervalued_probe.prompt: When you feel undervalued, what do you usually do?

options.label: Work harder and hope it's noticed

harder_reframe.body: Working harder to be seen teaches people you'll do more for the same recognition. Being valued often starts with you naming what you want out loud — not performing until someone guesses.

withdraw_socratic.body: Withdrawing protects you from disappointment but also from being known. What would it cost to stay engaged and ask directly for what you need?

resent_socratic.body: Resentment is often a boundary that never got spoken. What's the request hiding underneath it?

career_action.prompt: Turn this into one small, concrete step you could take in the next 72 hours. Make it specific and finishable — a single conversation, a paragraph written, a question asked. Not 'figure out my career.'
suggestions: Write one honest paragraph about what you'd change, for your eyes only.
Ask one person you trust the question you've been avoiding.
Block 25 minutes to start the smallest version of the thing.
Say the sentence you've been rehearsing to the person who needs to hear it.

close.body: You got to a real question and a real step — that's the whole job for today. Come back when it's done, and we'll take the next honest step from there.
